newsitem.title: USA: First Team optimistic on FY98 profits.
newsitem.headline: First Team optimistic on FY98 profits.

text.p: First Team Sports Inc said it is optimistic about another profitable year in fiscal 1998, despite continuing maturing of the in-line skate market and lower fiscal first-quarter sale versus the year-ago period.

"Although we are experiencing more seasonality and maturing of the in-line industry, we believe our strategy to gain market share and increase revenues through introduction of unique products and diversification of our product line, is the right strategy," said president John Egart.

On Wednesday, the company reported net sales for the first quarter ended May 31 were $26 million, compared to $30.6 million for the same period last year. Net income for the quarter was $1.9 million, versus $2.9 million in the comparable year-earlier quarter, First Team said.

"The in-line skate market is still feeling the effects of some excess inventory in the marketplace, and this, coupled with poor spring weather conditions in some key retail areas in the U.S. and Europe, kept sales below the prior year's first quarter," Egart said.
First Team makes UltraWheels in-line skates.

"Looking forward to the second quarter, it is too early to comment on how ... spring booking orders will translate into re-order business. However, due to the excess inventory situation at retail last summer, we have seen some caution by retailers as they continue to tightly manage their inventories to insure clean retail shelves for holiday promotional orders. We believe this to be true, as we are already receiving stronger holiday orders than last year at this time," he said.

"We remain optimistic that these efforts, combined with continued tight controls on selling, general and administrative expenses, will allow First Team Sports to achieve another profitable year in fiscal 1998," he said.
